subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should iMessage fail closed before access control when a non-group inbound DM has sender equal to destination_caller_id but canonical peer recovery is not confident?
rationale: That choice trades possible dropped live DMs against allowing an ambiguous local-identity payload to reach pairing, allowlists, sessions, and replies as the wrong sender; automation cannot choose that security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Canonical repair plus fail-closed guard
options.body: Use canonical iMessage handle normalization to repair only a confidently different peer and drop/log suspicious ambiguous payloads before access control when repair is not confident.

options.title: Canonical repair only
options.body: Repair the clear peer cases with canonical normalization but preserve current delivery for ambiguous payloads, accepting a narrower fix with less drop risk.

options.title: Pause for more live proof
options.body: Keep the PR draft until a maintainer or contributor captures enough redacted live data to decide whether fail-closed behavior is necessary.

recommendation.title: Canonical repair plus fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Use canonical iMessage handle normalization to repair only a confidently different peer and drop/log suspicious ambiguous payloads before access control when repair is not confident.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most recent current-main owner touching the central iMessage files and can route the security-boundary choice to the right iMessage maintainers if needed.
